subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is observed when a small piece of sodium is added to water?
options: It turns the water bright blue
It fizzes, moves on the surface and releases hydrogen
questions.explain: Sodium reacts vigorously with water, fizzing as it produces hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, what happens to the copper oxide?
questions.explain: The copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced.

questions.q: Why are alloys such as steel usually harder than the pure metal?
options: Different sized atoms distort the layers so they cannot slide easily
The atoms are all identical and slide easily
questions.explain: Different sized atoms in an alloy distort the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide.

questions.q: Bronze is an alloy mainly of copper and which other element?
questions.explain: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

questions.q: How does galvanising protect iron from rusting?
options: By coating it with a layer of zinc
By adding carbon to the iron
questions.explain: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which acts as both a barrier and sacrificial protection.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is best described as:
questions.explain: Using OILRIG, Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.

questions.q: In a sacrificial protection system, the metal attached to iron must be:
questions.explain: A more reactive metal corrodes in preference to the iron, protecting it sacrificially.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium does not form an ore
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide and electrolysis must be used.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.

questions.q: Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace by reduction with which substance?
questions.explain: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon reduces iron oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the least reactive?
questions.explain: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, making it the least reactive listed.

questions.q: Which gas is produced when magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explain: Reactive metals react with dilute acids to produce a salt and hydrogen gas.
